newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prudential restructure costs 148 Australasian jobs.
newsitem.headline: Prudential restructure costs 148 Australasian jobs.

text.p: Prudential Corporation Plc on Wednesday outlined plans for a new streamlined structure of its operations in New Zealand and Australia, less than a month after taking over life company New Zealand Insurance Life Limited.
"As a result of the restructuring 148 positions, including some contracting and temporary positions, have been made surplus," the company said in a statement.
Prudential said there would be no further redundancies in the next six months while it worked through the integration programme and made further decisions on structure over the next 18 months.
It added that the restructuring would initially create 37 new positions, which those people made redundant would be encouraged to apply for.

Prudential said it was now the third largest funds manager in New Zealand and was still on the acquisition trail, as part of Prudential's worldwide aim of becoming a dominant financial services company.
Managing director of Prudential Australia and New Zealand, Trevor Perry, said the driving force behind the changes was to create a leaner, more efficient organisation.
Prudential's head office will remain in Wellington and NZI Life's office in Queen Street will become Prudential's Auckland office.

"The centralising of underwriting, new business and client service functions to Auckland and Wellington from the 24 NZI Life branches will mean some branches may close. This area is currently being reviewed," Prudential said.
As announced in March by Prudential Portfolio Managers, there would be a single funds management team of 35 fund managers and analysts located in Sydney, Australia.
